tytul: Meadowsweet flower syrup: why there is no recipe here
wstep: There is no recipe here for syrup made from meadowsweet flowers (Filipendula ulmaria). [T:-]

ostrzezenia.tekst: According to a European Medicines Agency (EMA) monograph on meadowsweet flower as a traditional herbal medicine, it must not be used by people who are hypersensitive to salicylates; its use is not recommended in children and adolescents under 18 years of age or during pregnancy and breastfeeding, and using it together with salicylates or other NSAIDs is not recommended without medical advice. [T:SLO-487]

According to NDSU Extension, some flowers should not be eaten, so identify flowers correctly before eating them; flowers from a florist are meant to look at, not to eat, because some pesticides used on them have not been approved for edible plants. [T:SLO-489]

akapity: Herbs, flowers and infusions made from them are not naturally high-acid ingredients; to be canned, they need a tested recipe with an added amount of acid, sugar or both, even when the infusion is strained. [T:SLO-068]
According to Ask Extension, there are no research-based recipes for canning infused simple syrups. [T:SLO-481]
JarAtlas has found no tested recipe for meadowsweet syrup from a checked source. [T:-]
